thread:
incident-bot: PAGER: High tail latency + 503s in us-east for inference cluster. Pager duty triggered to #incidents.

emma (oncall): I'm seeing a big spike in 95/99 latencies, spike started ~03:41 UTC. Errors are mostly 503 / upstream timeouts. Dashboard: 503 rate ~4.8% across us-east-1.

sophia (eng-runtime): confirming - tail tokens CPU/GPU waiting looks elevated. KV cache evictions up, queue depth for gpus-4 is high.

raj (eng-sre): tagging. Can you paste the top error logs?

emma (oncall): paste logs below:

```
2026-03-15T03:41:02Z ERR route=generate backend=us-east-1 timeout=30s status=503 request_id=abc123
2026-03-15T03:41:06Z WARN queue_depth=42 pool=gpu-4 avg_lat=1320ms
2026-03-15T03:42:10Z INFO cache_miss=high client=partner-a
```

ben (prod-platform): Looks like one host in us-east started throttling requests to provider B. Provider B is flapping at the same time. We should consider short-term traffic shaping and provider reroute.

ana (support-lead): (reaction :exclamation:) We have 7 enterprise customers reporting elevated error rates via status page. Some on strict SLAs.

emma (oncall): I'm going to enable an emergency rate cap on non-enterprise tenants in us-east to reduce queue pressure. Proposed: global per-tenant qps cap -> 2 qps for free tier, 8 qps for standard, enterprise unchanged. Anyone objections?

raj (eng-sre): +1. Also suggest disabling background embeddings to lower avg token throughput. That's a quick toggle in FF.

emma (oncall): Doing the toggles now.

incident-bot: ACTION: feature-flag toggle by emma executed: disable=background-embeds scope=us-east roll=immediate

emma (oncall): rate caps applied via routing layer:
```
curl -X POST "https://ops-api/rate-limits" -d '{"region":"us-east-1","profile":"free","qps":2}'
```

sophia (eng-runtime): Seeing queue depth drop from 42 -> 18 in ~2m. Latency 95p improved from 1320ms -> ~720ms. 503 rate down to 1.2%. Good signal.

raj (eng-sre): Still seeing occasional flaps on provider B. Recommend a provider reroute for new sessions: prefer provider A for us-east with automatic fallback to B only if A errors <0.5% in last 2m. We can keep existing long-lived sessions pinned.

ben (prod-platform): I'll flip routing policy to prefer provider A for new sessions. Making the change now.

incident-bot: ROUTE_CHANGE by ben: prefer_provider=provider-a region=us-east scope=new_sessions

emma (oncall): Noting customer impact: estimated 14% of overall traffic affected by rate caps (mostly free + standard), enterprise unaffected. Notifying support.

ana (support-lead): Notifying customers now with templated update: "We're mitigating elevated error rates in us-east; non-enterprise flows are temporarily rate-limited and noncritical features disabled. Enterprise SLAs are unaffected."

sophia (eng-runtime): Quick check: KV cache miss rate is stabilizing. GPU queue depth per-host now ~10. Memory pressure lower.

raj (eng-sre): Plan for next 30m: 1) Monitor error rate and latency for 10m windows. 2) If error <0.5% and latencies stable, gradually lift rate caps over 20m. 3) If provider B still unstable, consider partial regional failover: shift 20-40% of new sessions to us-west w/ warmup nodes. Anyone want to take on the failover playbook?

ben (prod-platform): I can lead the partial failover. Will prepare warmup and route weights.

emma (oncall): I'm going to hand off on-call to raj at 04:05 UTC — need a short break. raj, you own the incident from here. Will keep monitoring in background.

raj (eng-sre): Acknowledged. Taking over at 04:05 UTC. Summary for handoff: rate caps applied (free/standard), background-embeds disabled in us-east, provider-a preferred for new sessions, enterprise traffic unchanged. Current metrics: 95p 720ms, 503 0.9%, queue depth avg 9.

incident-bot: HANDOFF recorded: from=emma to=raj at=1968072545

raj (eng-sre): Starting continuous checks. First rule: if 503 >1% for 3 consecutive 2-min windows, trigger partial regional cutover (20% shift to us-west). Second rule: if tail lat >1s for 5m, increase caching eviction budget.

sophia (eng-runtime): Also enabling a temporary lower token limit for non-enterprise prompt-lengths: max_tokens=512 (was 2048) in us-east only. That will reduce average generation time per request.

emma (oncall): Good. One more ask: engineering to create a postmortem timeline once stabilized and track customer incidents count.

ben (prod-platform): Starting weight shift to us-west for new sessions (0% -> 20%) in 5 steps over 10m. Executing now.

incident-bot: ROUTE_WEIGHT_CHANGE by ben: us-east=80%, us-west=20% scope=new_sessions staged=5

raj (eng-sre): Observing effects: 503 now 0.6%, 95p ~680ms. No new customer alerts. Continue monitoring. If stable for 15m, we'll begin rolling back the noncritical feature toggles and restore token limits gradually.

ana (support-lead): Support queue trending down. Customers from earlier alerts acknowledge the update.

raj (eng-sre): 15m check passed. Beginning controlled rollback: restore token limit to 1024 for standard, re-enable background-embeds for enterprise only, keep free tier cap at 2 qps until morning. Rolling changes in 3 steps.

sophia (eng-runtime): Rollback notes: enabling background-embeds for enterprise only:
```
ffctl set background-embeds=true --scope=us-east --plan=enterprise
```

incident-bot: FEATURE_TOGGLE by raj: background-embeds=enterprise-only region=us-east

raj (eng-sre): Final status at 04:23 UTC: 503 ~0.4%, 95p 610ms, queue depth avg 6, route weights us-east 85% / us-west 15% (holding). Incident severity -> reduced. Creating incident doc and postmortem action items.

emma (oncall): Thanks team, good handoff. I'll file customer followups for the enterprise ones and coordinate SLA notes.

ana (support-lead): I'll send the status page clear once we hit under 0.5% for 30m.

ben (prod-platform): Follow-up item: add stricter provider health gating to prevent provider B flaps from impacting queueing in a single region. I'll own that.

sophia (eng-runtime): Postmortem items: tune eviction thresholds, add automatic short token cap as a graceful degradation lever.

raj (eng-sre): Closing in monitoring but leaving this thread open for postmortem drafts. Good job. :thumbsup:
